claim.claim-text: 2. The method of claim 1 wherein: the preoperative face of the patient is continually scanned to update said preoperative face Input Data captured by the facial recognition system to thereby update in real-time the first visualization of the postoperative face of the patient.

3. The method of claim 1 further comprising: enabling the user to modify the first procedure plan; and generating a modified visualization of the postoperative face of the patient in a computer memory based on modification of the first procedure plan by the user.

4. The method of claim 3 wherein: the first procedure plan includes surgical markings; and further comprising generating a visualization of a preoperative face of the patient with surgical markings shown overlaid on top of the preoperative face of the patient by use of the AI Engine module; and wherein modification of the first procedure plan by the user includes modification to the surgical markings.
5. The method of claim 1 wherein: the first procedure plan includes surgical markings.

6. The method of claim 5 further comprising generating a visualization of a preoperative face of the patient with generated surgical markings shown overlaid on top of the preoperative face of the patient by use of the AI Engine module.

7. The method of claim 1, further comprising: after the step of generating the first visualization of the postoperative face of the patient, enabling the user to modify the postoperative patient's face; and generating a modified procedure plan based on the modification to the postoperative face of the patient.

10. The computing system of claim 1 wherein: after the step of generating the first visualization of the postoperative face of the patient, the at least one computer processor is configured to enable the user to modify the postoperative face of the patient; and wherein the at least one computer processor is configured to generate a modified procedure plan based on the modification of the postoperative face of the patient.

11. The computing system of claim 9 wherein: the preoperative face of the patient is continually scanned to update said preoperative Input Data captured by the facial recognition system to thereby update in real-time the first visualization of the predicted postoperative face of the patient.

12. The computing system of claim 9 wherein: the at least one computer processor is configured to enable the user to modify the first procedure plan; and wherein the at least one computer processor is configured to generate a modified visualization of the predicted postoperative face of the patient in computer memory based on modification of the first procedure plan by the user.
14. The computing system of claim 9 wherein: the first procedure plan includes surgical markings.

15. The computing system of claim 14 wherein: the at least one computer processor is configured to generate a visualization of the preoperative face of the patient with generated surgical markings shown overlaid on top of the preoperative face of the patient by use of the AI Engine module.

19. The computing system of claim 8 wherein: the computer memory stores instructions that, when executed by the at least one computer processor, causes the at least one computer processor to perform operations, including: after the first procedure plan is executed on the preoperative face of the patient to form the actual postoperative face of the patient, receiving postoperative feedback at the AI Engine Module; wherein the post operative feedback includes postoperative results programmed to be uploaded to the AI Engine module at predefined time intervals; and wherein the AI Engine module uses the postoperative feedback to refine the at least one artificial intelligence model.

20. The computing system of claim 8 comprising: the computer memory stores instructions that, when executed by the at least one computer processor, causes the at least one computer processor to perform operations, including: physically marking in ink on a physical face of the patient by use of a marking device, without user intervention, to mark in ink the first procedure plan on the physical face of the patient.
